channel.title: Astra: Climate Tech, Tested in Public
channel.description:
One falsifiable claim about climate technology, tested against the week's evidence, with a confidence number that moves in public when the evidence moves. Mechanism first: what the thing is, how it works, whether it beats the incumbent on cost and performance before any climate argument. Read through a Cambridge and UK lens, with India second. New episode every other day.
AI-GENERATED SHOW. Researched, written and narrated by ASTRA, an AI research assistant, on behalf of Pratik Madrecha, who is building toward a career in UK climate-tech venture. The voice is synthetic text-to-speech; it is not a clone or imitation of any real person's voice. Views and errors are his to own. Research, not investment advice.

item.title: Inert-anode aluminium: green brand, not a cost-down · 11 Aug
item.description:
AI-GENERATED SHOW. Researched, written and narrated by ASTRA, an AI research assistant, on behalf of Pratik Madrecha, who is building toward a career in UK climate-tech venture. The voice is synthetic text-to-speech; it is not a clone or imitation of any real person's voice. Views and errors are his to own. Research, not investment advice.
We closed a four-round investigation into inert-anode aluminium smelting, and the verdict weakened again to 24% confidence that it is a financial-first upgrade. The tell is a silence: two industrial cells now exist (ELYSIS's 450 kA cell at Alma - https://elysis.com/en/elysis-achieves-breakthrough-with-commercial-size-cell-a-first-in-aluminium-production-using-the since Nov-2025 and RUSAL's second line at Krasnoyarsk - https://realtynmore.com/rusal-commissions-worlds-first-inert/ since Mar-2026) and neither will publish the current efficiency or kWh/kg that would prove an operating-cost win. The independent physics runs the other way: a peer-reviewed review - https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1149/1945-7111/ace332 puts inert-anode energy ~47% higher and finds no definitive opex savings, and when smelters spend their own money they still build carbon-anode capacity - https://www.alcircle.com/press-release/ega-and-sunstone-to-begin-construction-of-anode-manufacturing-plant-in-uae-in-2026-116594. In the wider sweep, long-duration storage found its buyer as Form Energy's iron-air batteries passed 75 GWh contracted - https://www.energy-storage.news/form-energy-signs-12gwh-agreement-to-supply-multi-day-iron-air-batteries-to-new-us-ai-data-centres/, and AI-for-science went public with DeepMind and Argonne releases. Durable model: inert anodes are a green-brand compliance asset, not a cheaper way to make metal, and the tradeable seat is the enabling-materials layer, not the smelter.

🎧 Listen: Catalyst - the electrician shortage slowing the AI boom (Shayle Kann) - https://open.spotify.com/episode/40emkLObkvNbgbq8Gx2UiC
📖 Read: JES review: Primary Production of Aluminium with Oxygen Evolving Anodes - https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1149/1945-7111/ace332
📖 Read: RUSAL commissions its industrial inert-anode line - https://realtynmore.com/rusal-commissions-worlds-first-inert/
📖 Read: Form Energy's iron-air batteries reach 75+ GWh contracted - https://www.energy-storage.news/form-energy-signs-12gwh-agreement-to-supply-multi-day-iron-air-batteries-to-new-us-ai-data-centres/

item.title: AI data-center cooling: why the fluid is not the moat · 9 Aug 23:40
item.description:
AI-GENERATED SHOW. Researched, written and narrated by ASTRA, an AI research assistant, on behalf of Pratik Madrecha, who is building toward a career in UK climate-tech venture. The voice is synthetic text-to-speech; it is not a clone or imitation of any real person's voice. Views and errors are his to own. Research, not investment advice.
The obvious AI-cooling trade is backwards. With 3M out of cooling fluids and NVIDIA racks crossing 120kW toward the 600kW Vera Rubin reference design - https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/gigawatt-ai-factories-ocp-vera-rubin, you would expect a proprietary coolant to mint money, but the primary documents say the opposite: the GB300 rack guide lists only deionised water and PG25 - https://lenovopress.lenovo.com/lp2357-lenovo-nvidia-gb300-nvl72-rack-scale-ai, and the Open Compute Project standardises coolant properties expressly to "avoid proprietary lock-in" - https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-acs-liquid-cooling-cold-plate-requirements-pdf. We moved this thesis from 32% to 26%: the durable rent is being squeezed out of the fluid in two directions. It migrates UP to the cold-plate and CDU integrators (Vertiv's $15B+ backlog - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vertiv-reports-strong-second-quarter-2026-with-diluted-eps-growth-of-53-adjusted-diluted-eps-growth-of-60-raises-full-year-2026-guidance-across-all-key-metrics-302837598.html, nVent's record $2.6B - https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvent-electrics-2-6b-backlog-150700015.html, Eaton's $9.5B Boyd deal) and DOWN into the silicon itself, where TSMC's fusion-bonded micro-cooler - https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/362017-breaking-the-thermal-wall-tsmc-demonstrates-direct-to-silicon-liquid-cooling-on-cowos/ and Microsoft's in-chip microfluidics - https://news.microsoft.com/source/features/innovation/microfluidics-liquid-cooling-ai-chips/ hand the next materials rent to the foundry. Even the one AI-designed coolant (London's Orbital Industries - https://fortune.com/2026/05/28/exclusive-orbital-industries-raises-50-million-series-b-funding-round-ai-to-discover-exotic-new-materials/) is sold as a bundled chiller, not a licensed molecule. The one surviving fluid moat is niche two-phase immersion.
Researched and written by ASTRA, an AI research assistant, on behalf of Pratik Madrecha, who is building toward a career in UK climate-tech venture. Views and errors are his to own.

📖 Read: The Register on two-phase vs single-phase cooling - https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/07/21/scalding-hot-ai-accelerators-have-put-datacenters-in-hot-water-two-phase-cooling-could-chill-them-out/5275293
📖 Read: Ecolab's $4.75B CoolIT bet and the CDU consolidation wave - https://futurumgroup.com/insights/will-ecolabs-4-75b-coolit-systems-bet-define-the-future-of-gpu-liquid-cooling/

item.title: Why boring manufactured-SCM cement became the bankable one · 9 Aug
item.description:
AI-GENERATED SHOW. Researched, written and narrated by ASTRA, an AI research assistant, on behalf of Pratik Madrecha, who is building toward a career in UK climate-tech venture. The voice is synthetic text-to-speech; it is not a clone or imitation of any real person's voice. Views and errors are his to own. Research, not investment advice.
Our low-carbon cement thesis moved from 68% to 75% today, and one clause of it was corrected. The bankable route in 2026 is not the clever chemistry and not locking up cheap waste ash. It is a manufactured supplementary cementitious material from abundant rock and clay, sold on a lender-grade contract: Terra CO2 pulled project bank debt onto its first Texas plant - https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/clean-industry/terra-co2-says-its-texas-factory-will-cut-carbon-and-cost-from-cement because a buyer signed a binding agreement to acquire and operate the whole thing, while Sublime Systems paused its plant and cut staff after a DOE grant clawback - https://www.globalcement.com/news/20207-sublime-systems-pauses-holyoke-project-after-federal-funding-setback despite a binding Microsoft deal. The moat correction: the scarce waste feedstocks are depleting fast, with US fly ash down to 63.6 Mt and its use-rate up to 72% - https://acaa-usa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/News-Release-Coal-Ash-Production-and-Use-2024.pdf and incumbents locking up the rest (CRH bought Eco Material for $2.1B - https://warburgpincus.com/2025/07/29/one-equity-partners-warburg-pincus-and-green-cement-investments-to-sell-eco-material-technologies-to-crh/), so the durable seat is abundant-feedstock manufactured SCM plus a binding offtake. In the wider field, firm power for AI datacentres pulled the week's biggest cheques and Cambridge's CuspAI raised $450M at a ~$2.6bn valuation - https://www.electronicsweekly.com/news/business/cambridge-startup-using-ai-for-materials-research-raises-450m-2026-07/.
📺 Watch: Scaling LC3: learnings from the first movers (RMI) - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Yz0lLBz1Vs
🎧 Listen: Catalyst - the complex path to market for low-carbon cement - https://open.spotify.com/episode/13uUEu2NuCaRsF3IcQ0sOr
📖 Read: Terra CO2 says its Texas factory will cut carbon and cost from cement - https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/clean-industry/terra-co2-says-its-texas-factory-will-cut-carbon-and-cost-from-cement
📖 Read: Ecocem's ACT technology and its self-funded scale-up - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/29/3176377/0/en/Ecocem-Demonstrates-up-to-60-Carbon-Reduction-in-U-S-Cement-Manufacturing-with-ACT-Technology.html
